package_info.package_versions: Multiple versions affected by zero-day vulnerabilities (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The Struts2 package contained critical vulnerabilities that allowed remote code execution (RCE), enabling attackers to compromise web applications and directly access sensitive customer data. Attackers exploited these flaws to steal 143 million consumer records from Equifax.

execution_context.file_location: Core Struts2 request handling classes (e.g., Jakarta Multipart parser, OGNL expression evaluation)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Attacker-supplied HTTP request with malicious OGNL expression, e.g.:
Content-Type: %{(#_='multipart/form-data').
(#dm=@ognl.OgnlContext@DEFAULT_MEMBER_ACCESS).
(#_memberAccess?((#_memberAccess=#dm)):((#container=#context['com.opensymphony.xwork2.ActionContext.container']).
(#ognlUtil=#container.getInstance(@com.opensymphony.xwork2.ognl.OgnlUtil@class)).
(#ognlUtil.getExcludedPackageNames().clear()).
(#ognlUtil.getExcludedClasses().clear()).
(#context.setMemberAccess(#dm)))).
(@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec('id'))}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code evaluates attacker-supplied OGNL expressions in HTTP headers, leading to arbitrary command execution on the server and potential exfiltration of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Evaluating user-supplied expressions in a privileged context is highly dangerous and enables arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to treat HTTP headers as data, not executable code. The actual behavior allows attackers to inject and execute system commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL is legitimately used for data binding and expression evaluation in web frameworks, but never with untrusted input.
key_indicators: OGNL expression evaluation on untrusted input
Ability to execute arbitrary system commands
Modification of security context (e.g., member access)

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends specially crafted HTTP request containing malicious OGNL expression.
attack_chain.leads_to: OGNL expression is evaluated by Struts2 framework.

attack_chain.action: OGNL expression disables security restrictions and executes arbitrary system commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses RCE to access and exfiltrate sensitive data (e.g., consumer records).
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breach and loss of customer data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected OGNL expression evaluation from HTTP headers or parameters
Runtime execution of system commands (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec) triggered by web requests
Modification of OGNL member access or security context at runtime
file_indicators: Struts2 core classes handling multipart requests or OGNL evaluation
Unusual modifications to struts.xml or related configuration files
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with suspicious Content-Type or parameters containing OGNL syntax
Outbound connections or data exfiltration following web request processing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web application logs for OGNL expressions in HTTP headers or parameters, especially those attempting to modify member access or execute system commands. Use application firewalls to block suspicious payloads. Audit for unexpected process execution by the web server user. Regularly scan for vulnerable Struts2 versions and apply security patches promptly.
